name: Luigi Romanelli
credentials: Chief surgeon, civil hospital of Barletta
observation: Personally examined hands, feet and side; reports and letters survive.

name: Amico Bignami
credentials: Full professor of medical pathology, Royal University of Rome
observation: Personally examined wounds; proposed an ordinary pathological/chemical explanation rather than endorsing a supernatural cause.

name: Giorgio Festa
credentials: Physician and surgeon in private practice, Rome
observation: Repeated direct examinations; examined side again during the 1925 hernia operation; rejected trauma/caustic injury as adequate explanations.

name: Angelo Maria Merla
credentials: Physician; socialist mayor of San Giovanni Rotondo, 1915–1919; friary physician
observation: Early limited inspection, reported through a government report and Placido; could not determine precise cause. Not equivalent to a recovered signed wound report.

name: Luigi Pancaro
credentials: Physician working in Foggia and with Casa Sollievo; described as an internist by Muse; later worked in Canada
observation: Signed reports; blood and clotting investigations, stained-cloth examination; directly inspected the left-hand stigma in 1955 and expressly did not inspect the others then.

name: Alberto Caserta
credentials: Radiologist from Foggia
observation: Performed hand/foot radiographs; role establishes skeletal imaging rather than a complete skin-wound examination. Sources differ between 13 and 14 October.

name: Francesco (Franco) Lotti
credentials: Physician; chief pediatrician, Casa Sollievo della Sofferenza
observation: Reported blood tests and radiology arrangements; filmed final Mass and analyzed visible hand signs. His conclusion about the later disappearance relies on others’ postmortem report.

name: Andrea Cardone
credentials: Physician in Pietrelcina; treated Pio from 1910
observation: Reported seeing and palpating hand perforations. Statement does not date the particular examinations; editor explicitly flags limits of the late recollection.

name: Giuseppe Sala
credentials: Pio’s physician; assistant in medical semiotics, University of Naples; mayor of San Giovanni Rotondo, 1966–1974
dates: Later life; postmortem 23 September 1968; statement 7 July 1969
observation: Present for direct postmortem inspection and photography. Explicitly says he had not directly inspected the living wounds; do not count him as an independent confirmation of their original depth.

name: Raffaello Carlo Rossi
credentials: Discalced Carmelite; Bishop of Volterra; Holy Office apostolic visitor; later cardinal
observation: Direct examination and sworn interrogation. Described bodily signs but no open tissue breaks at that examination; rejected a crude fraud interpretation.
locator: Castelli’s edition of the 1921 inquiry; Muse section 1.1

name: Benedetto Nardella da San Marco in Lamis
credentials: Capuchin provincial minister and Pio’s spiritual director
observation: Personally described hand/foot wounds and side wound in correspondence and provincial records.

name: Pietro da Ischitella (Domenico Paradiso)
credentials: Capuchin provincial minister, 1919–1924; qualifications in literature and law per biographical note
observation: Accompanied examinations; described direct observation of wounds; correspondence survives. Not a medical examiner.

name: Paolino da Casacalenda (Paolino Di Tommaso)
credentials: Capuchin priest; superior of the friary when wounds appeared
observation: Saw hands and other wounds; supervised daily bandage changes and signed the eight-day report.

name: Basilio da Mirabello Sannitico
credentials: Capuchin friar/priest; bandaging committee member
observation: Co-signed sworn eight-day report concerning wound condition and bleeding.

name: Ludovico da San Marco in Lamis
credentials: Capuchin friar/priest; bandaging committee member
observation: Co-signed the same report. Do not automatically merge with similarly named Lodovico da San Giovanni Rotondo in other sources.

name: Placido da San Marco in Lamis (Ferdinando Bux)
credentials: Capuchin priest; Pio’s classmate; former military hospital chaplain; friary vicar
observation: Photographed wounds 19 August 1919; described participation in bandaging and witnessing examinations. Some remembered dates/duration are corrected by editor.

name: Nazzareno d’Arpaise
credentials: Capuchin priest; former guardian at San Giovanni Rotondo and guardian at Sant’Anna, Foggia
observation: Personally described exposed side wound.

name: Alberto Costa
credentials: Bishop of Melfi and Rapolla
observation: Reported seeing and kissing stigmata; letter dated 14 September.

name: Anselm Edward John Kenealy
credentials: Capuchin; Archbishop of Simla, India; former philosophy lecturer in England
observation: Expressly says he closely examined hand stigmata and interviewed Pio; ecclesiastical rather than medical examination.

name: Ignazio da Jelsi (Salvatore Testa)
credentials: Capuchin priest; guardian 1922–1925; provincial secretary and treasurer 1925–1959
observation: Diary describes assisting at hernia operation, seeing side wound, and bloodstained socks.

name: Fortunato da Serracapriola (Vincenzo De Marzio)
credentials: Capuchin priest; missionary in Eritrea; assisted Pio during liturgy and postoperative care
observation: Repeated close observations of bleeding hands during Mass; expressly had not seen bare foot wounds or side wound.

name: Emilio da Matrice (Pietro D’Amato)
credentials: Capuchin priest; a seminary pupil at the friary in 1918
observation: Described seeing new palm wounds and later kissing wounded palms.

name: Carmelo Durante da Sessano (Giovanni Durante)
credentials: Capuchin priest; friary superior 1953–1959
observation: Observed stained dressings and reduced blood output; arranged medical care and imaging.

name: Raffaele da Sant’Elia a Pianisi (Daniele D’Addario)
credentials: Capuchin priest; friary superior 1928–1941; Pio’s confessor
observation: Reported repeatedly seeing bleeding hands; present at postmortem observation and authenticated photographs.

name: Alessio Parente (Antonio Parente)
credentials: Capuchin friar/priest; personal assistant
observation: Personally cleaned bloody hands and described lesions; not a trained medical measurement of depth.

name: Carmelo Di Donato da San Giovanni in Galdo (Giuseppe Di Donato)
credentials: Capuchin priest; friary superior 1964–1969; provincial delegate
observation: Saw hands during Mass and examined body after death; commissioned and authenticated photographs. Distinct person from Carmelo Durante.

name: Pellegrino Funicelli da Sant’Elia a Pianisi (Ottavio Funicelli)
credentials: Capuchin priest; assistant, especially at night; heard final confession
observation: Saw side wound once, observed hands repeatedly, described later foot changes and postmortem absence of wounds/scars.

name: Donato da Welle
credentials: Capuchin Minister General 1938–1946; former rector of Ethiopian College, Vatican
observation: Explicitly says he examined stigmata; repeated visits and assessment of conduct.

name: Eusebio Notte (Nicola Notte)
credentials: Capuchin priest; Pio’s personal assistant 1960–1965
observation: Personally saw side wound while changing clothing after Pio’s fall.

name: Giacomo Piccirillo da Montemarano
credentials: Capuchin priest; friary’s designated photographer
observation: Direct postmortem observer and photographer of hands, feet and side; had never seen living side wound. Editor says chest photos miss its precise former location.

name: Marcellino Iasenzaniro
credentials: Capuchin priest; assistant and English-language correspondent in 1965; provincial councillor
observation: Saw wounded hands and later feet without visible dorsal wounds; expressly did not inspect soles then.

name: Giuseppe Orlando
credentials: Catholic priest from Pietrelcina; adviser/accountant/secretary for the hospital undertaking, 1946–1948
observation: Personally saw and handled wounded right hand; could not complete attempted depth assessment because of pain.

name: Elena Bandini
credentials: Lay Franciscan Third Order organizer from Borgo San Lorenzo
observation: Saw and kissed hand stigma; repeated Mass observations; also fragrance testimony.

name: Nina (Maria Annina) Campanile
credentials: Schoolteacher in San Giovanni Rotondo; early spiritual daughter
observation: Reported seeing new dorsal right-hand sign, having seen no sign on 18 September.

name: Vittoria Ventrella
credentials: Laywoman from San Giovanni Rotondo; early spiritual daughter
observation: Described visiting after sister’s report and Pio hiding wounds. Sister’s first-day observation is secondhand in her text.

name: Rina Giordanelli
credentials: Lay witness from Terni; called dottoressa in source, but field of degree/medical licensure not verified
observation: Described earlier wounded hands, later fading, and blood on final Mass days. Do not translate dottoressa alone into physician.

name: Elia Stelluto
credentials: Professional photographer, San Giovanni Rotondo
observation: Photographed final Mass; Lotti identifies specific negatives. Record includes a cameraman’s account of his presence, not a recovered separate written wound examination by Stelluto.

name: Mariano da Santa Croce di Magliano
credentials: Capuchin friar/priest; personal assistant
observation: Named by Carmelo, Pellegrino and Sala as present at postmortem observation; separate signed account not recovered here.

category: Additional reported witnesses and scope to verify
name: Guglielmo Sanguinetti
credentials: Physician; major collaborator in establishing Casa Sollievo
observation: Carmelo Durante attributes an opinion about changes in wound bleeding to him. Original signed wound inspection not recovered.

category: Additional reported witnesses and scope to verify
name: Giuseppe Bastianelli
credentials: Physician/professor; described in later accounts as physician to Benedict XV
observation: Reported examination in biographical/chronological sources; original wound report not recovered. Keep separate from signed reports above.
locator: Caccioppoli examination compilation; Servants of Suffering biography

category: Additional reported witnesses and scope to verify
name: Onorato Marcucci da San Giovanni Rotondo
credentials: Capuchin priest; personal assistant
observation: Pellegrino includes him among assistants noticing diminishing blood on side dressings. Own specific wound testimony remains retrieval target.
locator: 35; p. 125; official Padre Pio TV profile

category: Additional reported witnesses and scope to verify
name: Filomena Ventrella
credentials: Laywoman; sister of Vittoria
observation: Vittoria says Filomena first noticed red hand signs. This is an attributed witness, not a separately recovered statement.

category: Additional reported witnesses and scope to verify
name: Bonaventura Cerretti
credentials: Titular Archbishop of Corinth; Vatican secretary for Extraordinary Ecclesiastical Affairs; later cardinal
observation: Visit and request to examine wounds recorded; exact completed examination requires fuller original record. Sources disagree on precise May date.
locator: Official Padre Pio portal; later biographies

category: Additional reported witnesses and scope to verify
name: Luigi Besi
credentials: Passionist priest; postulator and papal emissary
observation: Reported visit and favorable assessment. Do not equate visit with independently documented complete wound examination.

category: Additional reported witnesses and scope to verify
name: Angelo Poli (Police)
credentials: Capuchin bishop; ecclesiastical superior in Allahabad, India
observation: Favorable written impression of Pio; specific examination scope not established here.

category: Additional reported witnesses and scope to verify
name: Augusto Silj
credentials: Cardinal; prefect of Apostolic Signatura
observation: Visitor associated with card carrying side-wound drawing; not a recovered clinical examiner report.

category: Additional reported witnesses and scope to verify
name: Alberto Valbonesi
credentials: Bishop, identified in later source as titular Bishop of Memphis
observation: Favorable personal encounter; direct wound inspection not established.

category: Additional reported witnesses and scope to verify
name: Roberto da Nove di Bassano
credentials: Capuchin priest
observation: Reported observing life and conduct; direct wound inspection not established.

category: Additional reported witnesses and scope to verify
name: Agostino da San Marco in Lamis
credentials: Capuchin priest; spiritual director and confessor
observation: Diary passage in this collection reports Pio’s account of origin, not an independently witnessed moment of stigmatization. Additional firsthand wound passages require exact citation.

category: Additional reported witnesses and scope to verify
name: Giuseppe Maria da Sarezzano
credentials: Capuchin priest; former deputy/general-curia secretary
observation: Reports administrative history and conversations about examinations, including a conflicting secondhand bandage-seal account. Not counted as a direct examiner.

category: Additional reported witnesses and scope to verify
name: Zucchetti (first name not verified)
credentials: Archbishop identified in Kenealy’s report with Smyrna/Trebizond titles
observation: Accompanied Kenealy; own wound inspection not established by that fact.

category: Additional reported witnesses and scope to verify
name: Antonio da Tasson
credentials: Capuchin general definitor for English-speaking provinces
observation: Accompanied Kenealy; own wound inspection not established.

category: Additional reported witnesses and scope to verify
name: Lorenzo da San Marco in Lamis
credentials: Capuchin guardian/superior; witness in Rossi inquiry
observation: Interview and temperature/fragrance testimony; specific wound-observation passages need recovery from full inquiry.

category: Additional reported witnesses and scope to verify
name: Luigi da Serracapriola
credentials: Capuchin friar; witness in Rossi inquiry
observation: Interviewed; direct wound inspection not established from retrieved summary.

category: Additional reported witnesses and scope to verify
name: Romolo da San Marco in Lamis
credentials: Capuchin friar; witness in Rossi inquiry
observation: Interviewed; direct wound inspection not established from retrieved summary.

category: Additional reported witnesses and scope to verify
name: Lodovico da San Giovanni Rotondo
credentials: Capuchin friar; witness in Rossi inquiry
observation: Interviewed; name differs from bandaging signatory Ludovico da San Marco in Lamis. Do not merge without checking originals.

category: Additional reported witnesses and scope to verify
name: Cherubino da San Marco in Lamis
credentials: Capuchin friar; witness in Rossi inquiry
observation: Character testimony recorded; direct wound inspection not established here.

category: Additional reported witnesses and scope to verify
name: Giuseppe Prencipe
credentials: Archpriest/canon, San Giovanni Rotondo
observation: Interviewed in inquiry; not automatically a wound examiner.

category: Additional reported witnesses and scope to verify
name: Domenico Palladino
credentials: Parish priest/canon and parish bursar, San Giovanni Rotondo
observation: Interviewed in inquiry; not automatically a wound examiner.

category: Additional reported witnesses and scope to verify
name: Agostino Gemelli
credentials: Franciscan priest, physician and psychologist; founder/rector of Catholic University of the Sacred Heart, Milan
observation: Important critic, but his own early report says no medical examination was performed. Do not count him among verified wound examiners.
locator: Muse quotation of 1920 report; Di Flumeri p. 95 editorial note

category: Additional reported witnesses and scope to verify
name: Michele Capuano
credentials: Physician, as identified by collection editor; precise institution not verified
observation: Commented on variation in wound descriptions; no personal wound examination established by that comment.
